preflight.note: Stamped by `repopact new`; the work item was recorded before implementation began.

acceptance_criteria.text: A real Windows NSIS/MSI installer is rebuilt from the current 3.1.2-based main tree (not WI062's 2026-09-12 pre-release build), installed, personally launch-verified, and uninstalled cleanly, matching WI062's own proof bar.

A real Linux .deb package is rebuilt from the current tree, installed, personally launch-verified (or verified via dpkg/desktop-integration inspection where a GUI session is unavailable), and uninstalled cleanly.

A signed Android release APK (or AAB) is built from the current tree using a real signing key (new or reused, operator-supplied), replacing WI062's debug build; the signing key material itself is never committed to the repository or evidence.

All three artifacts are explicitly shipped unsigned for Windows/macOS (no code-signing certificate acquired for this release); this is recorded as a deliberate operator decision, not an oversight, and the README/release notes disclose that Windows/macOS binaries are unsigned and may trigger SmartScreen/Gatekeeper warnings.

All built installer artifacts (Windows NSIS/MSI, Linux .deb, Android APK/AAB) are attached to a public GitHub Release for v3.1.3, alongside the existing PyPI wheel/sdist -- the first RepoPact release where these binaries are actually publicly downloadable rather than existing only as local build evidence.

README.md is updated with real download links/instructions for each installer artifact, keeping the existing PyPI-vs-full-source-tree distinction intact and not overclaiming platform support beyond what AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 actually proved (macOS/iOS remain undistributed).

No Tauri capability, CSP, filesystem, shell/process permission, WI050 admission, WI057 process guarantee, or WI059 validator authority is loosened to accomplish packaging; the Rust workspace tests, frontend typecheck/tests/build, and Tauri checks all pass on the exact tree the installers are built from.

RepoPact 3.1.3 is published through the normal governed release path (VERSION bump, decision record, repopact release build/verify for the Python package, twine-checked wheel/sdist, tag v3.1.3, PyPI publication, post-publication clean install) alongside the installer artifacts -- the Python package release is not skipped merely because installers are the headline of this release.
